journal phase; `npm run proof:purge` gained controls for each rule.

Key metadata is retained in the proposal file and counts toward its serialized
size limit; it is not copied into the created note.
The vault note-size check still runs before a new keyed proposal is staged; a
refusal leaves the key available, and a matching settled retry returns its receipt.

The [structured source-reference decision](https://github.com/kontourai/corpus/issues/46)
adds optional `provenance.source_refs` to create inputs. Session transcript
references carry bounded, validated attribution through proposal storage and
record creation. They neither authorize transcript access nor constitute review
evidence; `note` remains free text. Both store profiles run the source-reference
survival and validation conformance vectors. Validation copies reference objects
before persistence, including arrays with inherited serialization hooks; it refuses
serialization that adds, removes or changes references. It rejects sparse arrays
and prevents shared caller objects from
generating excessive YAML aliases, while preserving aliases in unrelated fields.
Keyed retries bind the references: changed or omitted attribution conflicts.
The source-reference purge-scrub vector passes against real purge in both profiles.
Pending proposals, cascaded records and all tombstone shapes also drop the field;
the separate in-flight purge-journal expected failure remains.

Validation snapshots the reference-array length before copying so a changing
proxy cannot bypass the 256-entry bound.

Hand-edited vault frontmatter reads plain scalars in source-reference string
fields as strings, like other store string fields.

The vault's proposal-size estimate serializes validated `source_refs` with the
candidate, so attribution bytes count toward the note bound before a keyed or
unkeyed proposal is staged. The apply path enforces the final note bound again.

The [root-binding decision](https://github.com/kontourai/corpus/issues/47)
adds a host-verifiable adapter binding based on a canonical root and a scaffolded
identity marker. Both profiles have match, mismatch, alias and re-scaffolding
vectors. Existing unmarked roots require explicit initialization before a new
adapter can attest them; this preserves legacy vault reads without writing to
the vault. The host still authorizes the root. Initialization is an explicit host-authorized
write, even for a kit-v1 vault; it does not enable record mutation there.
Initialization publishes markers without replacing a concurrent scaffold and can
recover a matching temporary link left after a completed marker was published.
Additional hard links to the marker, including hard-link snapshots, make binding
checks fail closed. Remove the extra links and reconstruct the adapter to restore
the binding.

A purge-enabled adapter's root binding and marker survive purge and reindex;
both profiles test the real purge path and still reject a different root.

topics.title: Manifest reference
topics.markdown:
## Manifest reference

Each repository has a schema v2 `corpus.json` at its root. Corpus no longer reads the retired v1 `docs-kit.json`. If a `docs-kit.json` is present, alone or next to `corpus.json`, `check`, `build`, `locate`, `init`, and `mcp --repo` stop with exit `2` and say what to do: rename it to `corpus.json`, set `"schemaVersion": 2`, and add `purpose` and `builtOn`, or delete the leftover when a `corpus.json` already exists.

```json
{
  "schemaVersion": 2,
  "purpose": "Make process and execution state visible to users.",
  "builtOn": [],
  "product": "flow",
  "title": "Flow",
  "tagline": "Process transparency for agentic work",
  "repo": "kontourai/flow",
  "landing": "README.md",
  "documents": [
    { "source": "docs/getting-started.md", "section": "Start Here", "covers": ["src/cli/**"] }
  ],
  "topics": [
    { "id": "workflows", "title": "Workflows", "source": "docs/concepts.md#workflows" }
  ],
  "exclude": ["docs/plans/**"],
  "branch": "main",
  "selectionActions": { "primary": "ask" },
  "redirects": {
    "gates-and-route-back.html": "docs/gates.md#route-back",
    "releasing.html": "https://example.com/releasing"
  },
  "allowLocalPaths": ["docs/install-paths.md"]
}
```

| Key | Required | Meaning |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `schemaVersion` | yes | Exactly `2`. A manifest with `1` is refused (exit `2`). |
| `purpose` | yes | Non-empty sentence describing the promise to users. The exact sentence `corpus init` writes is refused by `check`. |
| `builtOn` | yes | Public-contract building blocks: `{ "product": "id", "via": "package or CLI (or non-empty array)", "for": "use" }`; may be empty. Optional `"evidence": "cli"` and bare `bin` describe command evidence (see below). |
| `product` | yes | Lowercase slug. It must equal the repository name in `repo`, because the site lives at `https://kontourai.github.io/<product>/` and the hub fetches `/<product>/docs-bundle.json`. |
| `title` | yes | Display name. |
| `tagline` | no | One line shown in the site header and on the hub. |
| `repo` | yes | `owner/name` on GitHub. |
| `landing` | no | Markdown rendered as the site's `index.html`. Default `README.md`. |
| `documents` | yes | Documents, in navigation order. Each entry has `source` (a `.md` path), `section` (the navigation group) and, optionally, `title`, `covers`, and `publish`. See [Bundle-only documents](#bundle-only-documents). |
| `topics` | no | Curated entry points for agents. Each has `id` (a lowercase slug), `title`, and `source`, which is either `path` or `path#anchor`. |
| `exclude` | no | Globs for `docs/**/*.md` files that are deliberately unpublished. |
| `redirects` | no | Old page URLs that moved, mapped to their new place. Each key is a site-relative `.html` path; each value is a published source (`path` or `path#anchor`) or an absolute `https://` URL. See [Redirects](#redirects). |
| `branch` | no | The default branch, for the site's **Edit** links (`https://github.com/<repo>/edit/<branch>/<path>`). Default `main`. It must be a valid git branch name (no whitespace, `..`, `~^:?*[\\`, leading `-` or `/`, or `.lock` component). |
| `selectionActions` | no | The [selection toolbar](docs/site-output.md#selection-toolbar). Its only key, `primary` (required in the object), is `"ask"` (the default) or `"challenge-issue"`: the action that leads the toolbar. |
| `decisions` | no | The [decision registry](docs/decisions.md): `{ "dir": "docs/decisions", "index": "<dir>/index.md", "adr": { "dir": "docs/adr" } }`, every key optional (`{}` uses the defaults). Present, it turns on the `decisions` gate; `adr` also freezes that numbered ADR directory against additions. |
| `allowLocalPaths` | no | Exact paths of documents (the landing page or `documents` sources) that may contain absolute home-directory paths, such as deliberate examples. The [paths gate](#check) skips them. No globs. |

The validation rules:

- Validation is strict. An unknown key at any level is refused.
- Every path is repository-relative, POSIX, and normalized. Absolute paths, `..` segments, and symlinks that resolve outside the repository are refused. Every source must exist.
- Documents are listed once. They may not repeat the landing page, and they may not match `exclude`.
- A document's title is its first Markdown H1 outside blockquotes and lists, else the text of the first raw-HTML `<h1>` that has text, else a front-matter `title`, else the file name without `.md`. A `title` on the `documents` entry overrides all of them in the navigation, the page `<title>`, and `docs-bundle.json`; it must be a non-empty string without leading or trailing whitespace.
- A topic `source` must point at the landing page or at a listed document, so it is published. Its `#anchor` must be a heading outside blockquotes and lists (any level, `#` through `######`), slugged by [github-slugger](https://github.com/Flet/github-slugger): lowercase, punctuation dropped, spaces become `-`, and repeated headings get `-1`, `-2`, and so on.
- A leading YAML front-matter block is stripped before checking, rendering, and bundling, and check failures still report the source file's line numbers. A block is front matter when line 1 is `---` (after a UTF-8 BOM, which is always dropped), a `---` or `...` line closes it within the first 2000 lines, and it holds at least one top-level key line (`key:` at column 0). Otherwise, such as a thematic break followed by prose and another `---`, the document is left as written. Only a simple `title: value` (optionally quoted) is read from it; there is no YAML parser.
- `publish`, when present, must be a boolean. It defaults to `true`.
- Each `allowLocalPaths` entry must be a normalized repository path that is exactly the landing page or a `documents` source, listed once. A glob, or any other path, is a manifest error.
- `covers` holds globs of the code a document describes; the [freshness gate](#check) uses them. A bare directory name such as `src/cli` means `src/cli/**`. A glob that matches no tracked file (`git ls-files`; every file outside git) fails the `covers` gate of `check`, because it could never mark its document stale. It does not block `build` or the MCP server.

Section names group the navigation in the order they first appear in `documents`.

### Bundle-only documents

A `documents` entry with `"publish": false` is an agent-facing document that is not published as a web page, such as an internal manual. It is still a document in every other way:

- `build` renders no page for it, and it is left out of the navigation and the landing cards. It is still in `docs-bundle.json`, so the MCP server serves it, and topics may point at it.
- Its bundle `url` is `https://github.com/<repo>/blob/<sha>/<path>` at the built commit.
- Its bundle `markdown` has every relative link made absolute, so the text stands alone for an MCP reader: a link to a published document becomes the page URL under `--base-url`, a link to anything else becomes its GitHub `blob` URL (`tree` for directories), an image or other embedded file (Markdown image, raw-HTML `src`, `srcset`, or `poster`) becomes `https://raw.githubusercontent.com/<repo>/<sha>/<path>` so it resolves to the file itself, and a `#fragment` alone gets the document's own blob URL. This covers Markdown links, images, reference definitions, and raw-HTML `href`, `src`, `srcset`, and `poster`. Code blocks and code spans are left as written. Topics taken from the document get the same rewritten Markdown, and their `url` is the blob URL plus `#anchor`.
- `check` runs every gate on it: links, anchors, topics, covers, freshness, and paths. Reachability counts it as listed.
- A published page that links to it gets its GitHub blob URL, as for any other repository file.
- A redirect cannot target it, because it has no page; that fails the `redirects` gate.

### Redirects

GitHub Pages cannot send HTTP redirects, so when a page URL changes (for example `/flow/gates-and-route-back.html` became `/flow/docs/gates-and-route-back.html` when a product moved to corpus), list the old path under `redirects` and `build` writes a stub page there. The stub refreshes to the target at once (`<meta http-equiv="refresh" content="0; url=...">`), names it with `<link rel="canonical">`, asks search engines not to index it (`<meta name="robots" content="noindex">`), and shows a plain link to it.

A meta refresh drops the URL fragment, so the stub also carries a small inline script, placed before the meta refresh, that redirects with `location.replace` and keeps the fragment: `old.html#section` lands on the target's `#section`. When the target names its own anchor (`docs/gates.md#route-back`), that anchor wins and the incoming fragment is dropped, because the manifest chose it and the old page's fragment may not exist on the new page. An incoming fragment applies only to a target without one, for source and `https://` targets alike. Without JavaScript, the meta refresh still redirects, without the fragment. The script is template output, not document content: the target is embedded as a JSON string with every `<`, U+2028, and U+2029 escaped, so it cannot close the script element.

- A key is the old page's path relative to the site root, such as `gates-and-route-back.html` or `adr/0001-x.html`. It must end in `.html` and must not start with `/` or contain `..`, `#`, or `?`.
- GitHub Pages serves `x.html` for a request to `/x`, so a key `x.html` also redirects the extensionless URL `/x`.
- A value is either a source path, optionally with `#anchor` (`docs/gates.md`, `docs/gates.md#route-back`), or an absolute `https://` URL, which the stub uses in its parsed, normalized form (`new URL(value).href`). A source must be the landing page or a listed document that is published (not `"publish": false`), and its `#anchor` follows the rules of the [links gate](#check): a heading slug, or an `id` or `name` in raw HTML.
- A source target becomes a relative URL from the stub's own directory, so `adr/0001-x.html` pointing at `docs/gates.md` refreshes to `../docs/gates.html`. Its canonical URL is absolute, under `--base-url`.
- A key must not be a page corpus generates (`index.html` or a document's `.html`), compared after Unicode NFC normalization and case folding, and must not need a directory where corpus writes a file, or the reverse. A key may appear only once in the file. A stub that would overwrite a copied image or media file fails `build` with exit `1`, because assets are known only after rendering.
- Malformed keys or values are manifest errors (exit `2`). A target that is missing, unpublished, or has an unresolved anchor, and a colliding or repeated key, fail the `redirects` gate (exit `1`).
- Redirects are not part of `docs-bundle.json`.

topics.title: Corpus check and its gates
topics.markdown:
### check

```sh
corpus check [--root dir] [--base <git-ref>] [--advisory] [--only <gates>] [--json]
```

`check` runs the gates below and reports every failure, not only the first.

- `--only <gates>` runs only the named gates, comma-separated, using the names in the list below (`builtOn`, `adr-freeze`, and so on). The manifest always runs, because every other gate depends on it. An unknown name is a usage error (exit `2`). So is a selected gate that does not run, such as `freshness` without `--base`, `decisions` without a `decisions` block, or `adr-freeze` without `--base` and `decisions.adr`: a lane that asks for one gate never passes by checking nothing. So is a flag that no selected gate reads: `--base` unless `freshness` or `adr-freeze` is selected, and `--advisory` unless `freshness` is, so a mistyped ref is never silently ignored. A gate that runs but has nothing to examine still passes: `--only manifest` runs only the manifest, and `--only freshness` passes in a repository whose documents declare no `covers`.
- `--json` prints one JSON object on stdout instead of the text report. Exit codes are unchanged. Whenever `--json` appears among `check`'s arguments, stdout holds exactly one JSON object, whatever happens. A run that does not reach a gate result still prints `{ "verdict": "fail", "exitCode": 2, "error": "…" }` (plus `schemaVersion`, `tool`, `command`, `base`, `advisory`, and `only`), with the message also on stderr. That covers an unknown option, an option with a missing or blank value, a bad `--only`, a missing `corpus.json`, and an unexpected internal error. `--help` prints text, so it cannot be combined with `--json`; together they are refused the same way. A gate result is:

  ```json
  {
    "schemaVersion": 1,
    "tool": "corpus",
    "command": "check",
    "verdict": "fail",
    "exitCode": 1,
    "base": "origin/main",
    "advisory": false,
    "only": ["freshness"],
    "summary": { "failures": 1, "warnings": 0, "errors": 0, "staleDocuments": 1 },
    "gates": [
      { "name": "manifest", "status": "pass", "failures": [], "warnings": [] },
      { "name": "freshness", "status": "fail", "note": "3 changed files since origin/main", "failures": ["docs/cli.md is stale: …"], "warnings": [] }
    ],
    "staleDocuments": [
      { "source": "docs/cli.md", "kind": "docs-covers", "gate": "freshness", "severity": "failure", "changed": ["src/cli.js"] }
    ],
    "actions": [
      { "type": "docs-covers", "description": "docs/cli.md is stale: 1 covered file changed since origin/main but the document did not", "paths": ["docs/cli.md", "src/cli.js"] }
    ]
  }
  ```

  `verdict` is `pass`, `warn` (exit `0` with warnings, as under `--advisory`), or `fail` (exit `1` or `2`; `exitCode` tells them apart). A gate's `status` is `pass`, `warn`, `fail`, `skip` (with `skipped`, the reason), or `error` (with `error`). `summary` holds only numbers. Every stale document carries the `kind` of staleness, never a bare stale flag. Today the only kind is `docs-covers`: a file matched by the document's `covers` changed and the document did not. `changed` lists every such file, and `severity` is `warning` under `--advisory`. `actions` has one entry per stale document, with `type` set to its kind. A broken link and a stale document therefore no longer look the same: both exit `1`, but only a stale document is listed in `staleDocuments` and `actions`. The shape matches the external-tool artifact that a [Veritas](https://github.com/kontourai/veritas) evidence check reads (`verdict`, numeric `summary`, `actions`), so `corpus check --base origin/main --only freshness --json` can be bound as evidence.

For v2 manifests, the **builtOn** gate compares declarations with root and workspace `package.json` dependencies, peer dependencies, and optional dependencies. Dependencies are verified by their exact package keys in `via`. `via` accepts a string or a non-empty array, allowing `{ "product": "console", "via": ["@kontourai/console-core", "@kontourai/console-ui"], "for": "Console integration" }`. All names in an entry are declared to belong to that product. **Product ids and package-to-product ownership are declared by the owner and cannot be verified offline.** The gate does not derive product identity from a scope, package name, or GitHub repository name. Missing-package suggestions use `OWNER_PRODUCT_ID`, which the owner must replace.

Kontour dependency recognition uses npm's package-spec parser. Scoped `@kontourai/*` package keys count, except an `npm:` alias to a non-Kontour target does not. An alias such as `flow-alias: "npm:@kontourai/flow@^1"` counts, and **`via` must name the alias key (`flow-alias`), not the target package**. GitHub specs count when their owner is `kontourai` (case-insensitive): `github:kontourai/repo` (including `/subpath`), bare `kontourai/repo`, `git+https://`, `git+ssh://git@`, `git@github.com:`, `git://`, and `https://github.com/` forms. GitHub and `https://codeload.github.com/kontourai/repo/...` tarball URLs also count. Other owners/hosts and unscoped registry packages do not count. Workspace/link/patch protocols are not parsed as GitHub or npm aliases; a scoped package key still counts. This classification inspects specs without fetching or executing them.

Scoped dependencies whose keys match the root package name or any workspace member's package name are excluded: a repo's own packages are not building blocks. This uses `package.json` names, never a name prefix. A package or CLI named more than once in `via` fails, including repeats within one array. Each declared name is checked separately against dependencies or CLI evidence. Missing runtime declarations and phantom declarations exit `1` with a fix. Dev-only packages warn, whether declared or not; malformed package JSON or YAML evidence exits `2`. Workspaces support `package.json` directory globs (an array or `{ "packages": [...] }`) and a real YAML-parsed `pnpm-workspace.yaml` `packages` array, including indented/unindented block lists, flow arrays, and exclusions. An existing pnpm file takes precedence. A missing `packages` key, `packages: []`, a list of only `!` exclusions, or `packages: ['.']` means a single-package repo: only the root package is compared. `.` (or `./`) names the root package, which is always compared. A list with any other inclusion glob exits `2` if no workspace member package files resolve, even when it also lists `.`. A missing root `package.json` prints an explicit skip; v1 skips this gate.

A dependency-free declaration requires explicit `"evidence": "cli"` and a non-empty reason in `for`. Evidence is read from root/workspace package scripts, `.github/workflows/*.yml` / `*.yaml` `jobs.*.steps[*].run`, and composite `.github/actions/**/action.yml` / `action.yaml` `runs.steps[*].run` values. Nested `with.run`, step names, comments, quoted mentions in arguments, heredoc bodies (including quoted and tab-stripped delimiters), and non-composite actions do not count. Composite action files are scanned as invocation evidence even if the action is not referenced by a workflow; this does not prove reachability or execution.

Recognised shell forms are direct `<bin>`, `./node_modules/.bin/<bin>`, `npx [-y|--yes|--no-install|--] <bin>[@version]`, `npm exec [--] <bin>[@version]`, `pnpm exec [--]`, `pnpm dlx [--]`, `yarn exec [--]`, `yarn dlx [--]`, and `pnpm <bin>` / `yarn <bin>`. A version (`<bin>@1`) is accepted only after `npx`, `npm exec`, `pnpm exec`/`dlx`, and `yarn exec`/`dlx`; `pnpm <bin>@1`, `yarn <bin>@1`, and a direct `<bin>@1` are not evidence. Leading `VAR=value` assignments and shell separators/newlines are supported. Every `${{ … }}` expression is replaced with an unknown placeholder word before tokenisation, including quoted and unquoted expressions in scripts and steps. As in GitHub's own parser, an expression ends at the first `}}` outside a single-quoted string, so `${{ '}}' }}` is one expression. Scripts are tokenised one logical line at a time: physical lines joined by backslash continuations or by a quote still open at the line end, which is what the shell reads as one command line. A line the tokenizer cannot parse (a bad `${…}` substitution, or a `${{` that never closes) supplies no evidence, but other lines of the same script or step are still examined, and a heredoc started on it still hides its body. The line is not split at `;` or `&&`, because finding those needs the parsing that failed. When a CLI declaration then has no evidence, its failure says how many command lines were skipped as unparseable and names up to three as `<file> scripts.<name> line <n>` or `<file> jobs.<job>.steps[<i>].run line <n>`. A static executable with expression-valued arguments can qualify; an expression-valued executable cannot. Other wrapper flags, `npm run`, shell functions/control-flow syntax, dynamic command names, command substitutions, reusable workflow references, PowerShell and cmd.exe syntax are not interpreted. The check is textual POSIX-style command evidence, not proof that a command ran or succeeded.

If a scoped package's executable differs, use a bare `bin` string: `{ "product": "veritas", "via": "@kontourai/governance", "bin": "veritas", "for": "Check governance readiness", "evidence": "cli" }`. `bin` applies to every name in that entry for CLI evidence; it does not change package dependency matching. The check verifies the declared executable is invoked, not that a package actually publishes that executable.


1. **manifest:** `corpus.json` is valid, as described above. If it is invalid, the other gates are skipped and the exit code is `2`.
2. **links:** every Markdown link and image, and every raw-HTML `href`, `src`, `srcset`, and `poster` (double-quoted, single-quoted, or unquoted), in the landing page and the listed documents (bundle-only ones included) resolves. A reference to a file under `.git/`, through a symlink, or to an untracked or git-ignored file (such as `.env`), is an unpublishable reference and fails. Raw HTML is tokenized with htmlparser2, so HTML comments are ignored, an empty raw `href=""` is allowed, and `srcset` is parsed per the HTML spec, so `data:` URIs stay whole. Relative files must exist, with exact case. A `#anchor` must match a heading slug, or an `id` or `name` attribute in raw HTML, in the target `.md`. External `http(s)` links are not fetched. A leading `/` resolves from `--root` (which is the repository root unless you point `--root` at a subdirectory).
3. **reachability:** every `docs/**/*.md` is listed in `documents` (with or without `"publish": false`), is the landing page, or is matched by `exclude`. When the manifest declares `decisions`, every `*.md` directly in `decisions.dir` (the records and the index) also counts as reachable without being listed; the decisions gate checks them. They are published only if listed in `documents`.
4. **topics:** every topic anchor resolves to a heading outside blockquotes and lists.
5. **redirects:** every [redirect](#redirects) target is published and its `#anchor` resolves, and no key repeats or collides with a file corpus generates.
6. **paths:** no absolute home-directory path appears in the landing page or any listed document, bundle-only ones included: `/Users/<name>/`, `/home/<name>/`, or `C:\Users\<name>\` (any drive letter, either slash). The whole Markdown body is scanned as text, so prose, code, links, and raw HTML all count; front matter is not, because it is never published. Each hit is reported as `file:line`. A path inside a URL such as `https://host/home/x/` does not match, and neither does a placeholder name such as `<name>`, `$USER`, or `{user}`. Two non-personal directories are exempt: `/Users/Shared/` (the macOS shared folder) and `/home/runner/` (the GitHub Actions runner home). List a document in `allowLocalPaths` when it needs real example paths.
7. **purpose:** the manifest's `purpose` is not the exact placeholder sentence that `corpus init` writes. This gate fails with exit `1`, not `2`, so a new adopter still sees every other gate. It compares the whole sentence, not a `TODO` substring.
8. **covers:** every `covers` glob matches at least one tracked file. This gate fails with exit `1`.
9. **decisions:** only when the manifest declares `decisions`. Every record in `decisions.dir` is a valid [decision record](docs/decisions.md#record-format) and the index is what `corpus decisions index` would write. The directory is read directly, whatever `documents` and `exclude` say. Fails with exit `1`.
10. **adr-freeze:** only when the manifest declares `decisions.adr`. Without `--base` it is reported as skipped. A file added under `decisions.adr.dir` since the merge base fails with exit `1`, except a `README.md` or `index.md` directly in it. See [Numbered ADRs](docs/decisions.md#numbered-adrs).
11. **freshness:** this gate runs only with `--base`. It reads the changed files from `git diff --name-only --no-renames <base>...HEAD`, which diffs from the merge base and lists both paths of a renamed file. If a document's `covers` globs match a changed file, the document's own `source` must also be in the changed set. Otherwise the document is stale. With `--advisory`, stale documents are printed as warnings and the exit code is `0`. A base that does not resolve, or a directory that is not a git checkout, gives exit `2`, never a silent pass.

topics.title: Corpus build
topics.markdown:
### build

```sh
corpus build [--root dir] [--out dist-pages] [--base-url https://kontourai.github.io/<product>/]
```

`build` runs `check` without the covers, adr-freeze, and freshness gates and refuses to build if it fails. It then replaces `--out` with:

- `index.html` (the landing page), one page per published document (not [bundle-only](#bundle-only-documents) ones), and `docs-kit.css`. Every page has navigation grouped by section, a link to the hub at <https://kontourai.github.io/>, and a link to the repository. The landing page's `<title>` is `<title> — <tagline>`, or `<title> documentation` when there is no tagline. Long inline text wraps to the document column; wide code blocks and tables scroll within it.
- Links between published documents, rewritten to the generated pages, in Markdown and in raw HTML (`href`, `src`, `srcset`). Links to other repository files go to `https://github.com/<repo>/blob/<sha>/<path>`, or to `tree` for directories.
- Copies of the local images and embedded media (`src`, `srcset`, `poster`) that published documents reference. Inside git, only git-tracked files are copied, never anything under `.git/` or through a symlink, and each file is capped at 25 MB; a larger tracked file keeps its GitHub link. Assets are collected after sanitization, so a file referenced only by a stripped tag (`iframe`, `embed`, `script`, ...) is never copied.
- A selection toolbar on every page (`docs-kit.js`, a static template script): select text in the page content to copy an **Ask** or **Challenge** prompt for your agent with the source path, line range, and sha, open a prefilled GitHub issue, or open the source in GitHub's editor. Rendered blocks carry `data-src-line` with their source-file lines, and `<main>` carries the page's path, sha, and repository. Where the browser offers [WebMCP](docs/site-output.md#webmcp-tools), the script also registers in-page tools. See [the generated site](docs/site-output.md#selection-toolbar).
- Sanitized HTML. Every product site shares the `kontourai.github.io` origin, so rendered Markdown is reduced to GitHub-like output: no `script` or `style`, no `on*` attributes, and only `http(s)`, `mailto`, and image `data:` URLs.
- Mermaid diagrams. A fenced ` ```mermaid ` block becomes `<pre class="mermaid">` holding the escaped diagram source. Only pages with such a block load Mermaid, from jsDelivr, pinned to one version with an SRI `integrity` hash, with `securityLevel: 'strict'` and `htmlLabels: false` (labels are plain SVG text, so diagram HTML never bypasses the sanitizer), and a theme that follows `prefers-color-scheme`. That script is part of the page template; a `script` in the Markdown is still stripped. See [the generated site](docs/site-output.md#mermaid-diagrams).
- A redirect stub for each `redirects` key. See [Redirects](#redirects).
- `.nojekyll`, a `.docs-kit-build` marker, and `docs-bundle.json`. The bundle is described in [docs/bundle-format.md](docs/bundle-format.md#docs-bundlejson).

`build` then checks every internal `href` and `src` in the generated site, and the URL of each redirect stub's meta refresh, including `#fragments`, and exits `1` if any of them is broken. Each stub must also have exactly one redirect script whose target resolves and equals its meta refresh URL. `build` needs a git checkout because the bundle and the GitHub links carry `git rev-parse HEAD`. `--out` is resolved relative to the current directory and is deleted before each build. `build` refuses an `--out` that is the repository or a parent of it, is inside a `.git` directory, or contains git-tracked files. It also refuses any existing non-empty directory unless every file in it is listed in the `.docs-kit-build` manifest that a previous build wrote. This applies inside or outside git, whether or not the directory is ignored. A file added by hand blocks the rebuild, and the error names it. A new or empty directory is fine. A forged marker is trusted: corpus deletes whatever a marker lists.

topics.title: MCP server tools and sources
topics.markdown:
## MCP server

The server exposes six read-only tools. Every result carries the source commit `sha` of the bundle it came from, and `dirty: true` when a local checkout has uncommitted changes. A tool never throws: problems come back as results with `isError` set.

| Tool | Arguments | Returns |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `list_products` | none | product, title, tagline, sha, builtAt, siteUrl, topicCount, docCount (not counting the landing page); failed products are listed as `unavailable` |
| `list_topics` | `product?`, `parentId?` | topics with product, id, title, source, url, sha, and `parentId`, `tags`, and `summary` when the bundle has them; `parentId` lists only that topic's children, and an id that is no topic in the selected products is an error |
| `get_topic` | `product`, `id` | the topic's Markdown section |
| `get_document` | `product`, `source` | one whole document, including the landing page (`landing: true`) |
| `search` | `query`, `product?`, `limit?` (1-50, default 10) | ranked matches over topics and documents, with snippet, product, source, url, sha; topic matches also carry `parentId`, `tags`, and `summary` when present |
| `locate` | `product`, `quote`, `source?` | where a quoted passage lives: `source`, `repoPath`, 1-based file `startLine` and `endLine`, sha, the enclosing `heading` and `anchor`, the page `url`, the surrounding `markdown` blocks, a GitHub `blobUrl` ending in `#Lstart-Lend`, `match`, `confidence`, and, when the quote matches more than one place, `ambiguous: true`, `matchCount`, and up to 10 `alternatives` |

`locate` is what the site's Ask and Challenge prompts tell an agent to call. It compares letters and digits only, lowercased and with accents removed (NFKD), so whitespace, punctuation, and Markdown formatting (emphasis, code marks, link destinations, HTML tags, list and table markers, fence lines) do not matter. Numeric entities and `&`, `<`, `>`, `"`, `'`, and ` ` are decoded; other named entities (such as `é`) are ignored, so a quote containing their character falls back to the surrounding words. Text inside code blocks and code spans is compared as the page shows it, so `<dir>` in a code sample still matches. `match` is `verbatim` (confidence 1) when the quote also appears as written, `normalized` (0.9) when it matched only after that normalization, or `head-and-tail` (0.5) when only its first and last four words matched within a nearby window, for example across an image. With more than one candidate, the confidence is divided by their number (minimum 0.01); verbatim candidates rank before normalized ones, each in document order, and the best is returned with up to 10 others as `alternatives` and the total as `matchCount`. No match, a quote with fewer than 3 letters or digits, or an unknown `source` is an error result. Line numbers are file lines, after front matter; a bundle built before 0.6.0 does not record front matter, so `locate` adds a `note` saying it assumes none.

The server has four sources:

- `--repo dir` builds the bundle in memory from a checkout and writes nothing. It rebuilds whenever the checkout changes, so a long session sees current docs. The cache key is HEAD, a hash of `git status --porcelain`, and the mtime and size of the manifest and each published source. It needs a valid manifest and resolvable topics at startup; a later breakage is reported as unavailable.
- `--workspace dir` does the same for every immediate subdirectory that contains `corpus.json`. A subdirectory with only a retired `docs-kit.json` is skipped, with one note on stderr per server, so a stale checkout neither stops the workspace nor disappears silently; one with both files is reported as unavailable. It rescans the directory on every call and rebuilds only the products that changed. A subdirectory that fails is reported as unavailable under the `product` its manifest declares (the directory name if the manifest does not parse). If two directories declare the same product, both are unavailable.
- `--hub url` fetches `<url>/products.json` and then each `<url>/<product>/docs-bundle.json`. It keeps successful fetches in memory for 10 minutes and retries failed or malformed ones after 30 seconds. A product whose fetch fails, or whose bundle is malformed, is reported as unavailable; this is not fatal.
- `--bundle file` serves a prebuilt `docs-bundle.json` exactly as written: from `corpus build`, or from a host's own generator. Repeat it to serve more products. Each file is read and validated once at startup and held in memory; nothing is rebuilt, refetched, or reread, so results always carry the sha the bundle was built at. A malformed bundle, an unreadable file, or two bundles for the same product is a usage error (exit `2`). Programs that embed the server get the same source from `staticSource(bundles)`, passed to `createDocsServer`.

Claude Code:

```sh
claude mcp add kontour-docs -- npx -y --package=@kontourai/corpus@<version> -- corpus mcp
```

Codex (`~/.codex/config.toml`):

```toml
[mcp_servers.kontour-docs]
command = "npx"
args = ["-y", "--package=@kontourai/corpus@<version>", "--", "corpus", "mcp"]
```

To serve local checkouts while you write docs, add `--workspace ~/dev/github/kontourai` or `--repo .` after `mcp`.

topics.title: Hub site and product states
topics.markdown:
### hub

```sh
corpus hub [--products products.json] [--out dist-hub]
```

`hub` builds the organization hub: a self-contained `index.html` and a copy of `products.json`. It validates `products.json` strictly. Serve the output at the origin root (`https://kontourai.github.io/`), because each product card loads `/<product>/docs-bundle.json` from the same origin. Each card also loads `https://api.github.com/repos/<repo>/commits/HEAD` (the default branch), which it caches in `localStorage` for 10 minutes. Each card shows one state:

| State | Meaning |
| --- | --- |
| `unpublished` | The bundle could not be fetched. |
| `behind` | The bundle's `sha` differs from the default branch HEAD. The card shows the bundle's age and the HEAD commit's. |
| `thin` | The bundle has fewer than 3 documents, not counting the landing page. |
| `current` | The bundle's `sha` equals the default branch HEAD. |
| `unknown` | The GitHub API could not be read (for example, it was rate limited), so `current` cannot be claimed. |

If more than one state applies, the first one in the table wins.

topics.title: Adopting Corpus in a repo
topics.markdown:
## Adopting corpus in a repo

1. Add Corpus as an exact-pinned dev dependency and commit the lockfile, so CI installs the same Corpus and the same dependency tree every time. For an unreleased commit, use `https://codeload.github.com/kontourai/corpus/tar.gz/<sha>` (full sha) as the spec instead.

   ```sh
   npm install --save-dev --save-exact @kontourai/corpus@<version>
   ```

2. Scaffold and review the manifest. Replace the `purpose` placeholder (`check` fails until you do), fill `builtOn` (or leave it empty), order the documents, name the sections, move internal docs to `exclude`, and add `topics` and `covers`.

   ```sh
   npx --no-install corpus init
   npx --no-install corpus check
   ```

3. Add the gate to CI. On pull requests, `fetch-depth: 0` makes the base branch available for freshness. Drop `--advisory` once the `covers` globs are trusted.

   ```yaml
   - uses: actions/checkout@v7
     with:
       fetch-depth: 0
   - uses: actions/setup-node@v6
     with:
       node-version: 24
   - run: npm ci
   - run: npx --no-install corpus check
   - if: github.event_name == 'pull_request'
     run: npx --no-install corpus check --base origin/${{ github.base_ref }} --advisory
   ```

4. Publish Pages from `main`. Set the repository's Pages source to GitHub Actions, then run:

   ```yaml
   - run: npx --no-install corpus build --out dist-pages
   - uses: actions/upload-pages-artifact@v5
     with:
       path: dist-pages
   - uses: actions/deploy-pages@v5
   ```

5. Add the product to the hub's `products.json` (`{"product": "<repo>", "repo": "kontourai/<repo>"}`).

topics.title: Decision records and the ADR freeze
topics.markdown:
# Decision records

A decision registry keeps one living record per decision subject, in `docs/decisions/<topic-slug>.md`, plus a generated index. When the subject's answer changes, the record is edited; when the subject moves or is folded into another, the old record becomes a tombstone that names the new one. Git history and pull request review are the record's lifecycle.

Corpus checks the registry when `corpus.json` (schema v2) declares it:

```json
"decisions": { "dir": "docs/decisions", "index": "docs/decisions/index.md", "adr": { "dir": "docs/adr" } }
```

| Key | Default | Meaning |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `dir` | `docs/decisions` | The registry directory. Every `*.md` directly in it, except the index, is a record. It need not exist yet; `corpus decisions index` creates it. |
| `index` | `<dir>/index.md` | The generated index. It must be a `.md` file directly inside `dir`. |
| `adr` | absent | Optional. Declaring it freezes the numbered ADR directory `adr.dir` (default `docs/adr`), which must exist. See [Numbered ADRs](#numbered-adrs). |

`"decisions": {}` uses every default and leaves the ADR freeze off. Paths follow the [manifest path rules](../README.md#manifest-reference): repository-relative, POSIX, normalized, and inside the repository. `adr.dir` must not overlap `dir`. Unknown keys are refused, as everywhere in the manifest.

The gate reads `dir` directly. Whether the records are listed in `documents` or matched by `exclude` does not change what it checks; those keys only decide whether the records are published.

### Reachability and publishing

Once `decisions` is declared, every `*.md` directly in `dir`, records and index alike, counts as reachable for the [reachability gate](../README.md#check), so adding a record needs no `corpus.json` edit. A Markdown file in a subdirectory of `dir` is not a record and still has to be listed or excluded.

Reachable is not published. A record or the index appears on the site and in `docs-bundle.json` only when `documents` lists it, as for any other document; listing it with `"publish": false` puts it in the bundle without a page. Records are not published automatically, because that would change the site and the bundle digest of every repository that declares `decisions`, and many keep their records as contributor-facing history rather than product documentation.

A `documents` entry may name the index before it exists: `corpus decisions index` accepts that one missing file and writes it, so a repository can write its intended manifest first and generate the index second. Every other command, `corpus check` and `corpus decisions check` included, still fails on a listed index that does not exist (exit `2`), and `corpus decisions index` still refuses any other missing document.

## Record format

A record is a Markdown file whose YAML frontmatter starts at byte 0:

```markdown
---
status: current
subject: Release channels
decided: 2026-07-03
evidence:
  - kind: issue
    ref: https://github.com/kontourai/example/issues/310
  - kind: adr
    ref: docs/adr/0004-release-channels.md
---

# Release channels

The current answer, its rationale, and its boundary.
```

| Field | Required | Rule |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `status` | yes | One of the [statuses](#statuses). |
| `subject` | yes | A non-blank, single-line noun phrase naming the subject, with no control characters (it becomes a cell of the index table). Ideally a term from the repository's domain vocabulary; this is not checked. |
| `decided` | yes | `YYYY-MM-DD`: the date the current answer was ratified, or the date a `needs-decision` stub was recorded. |
| `evidence` | yes | A non-empty list of `{ kind, ref }`. See [Evidence](#evidence). |
| `supersedes` | no | A list of slugs of existing records whose subjects this record absorbed. |
| `superseded_by` | `superseded` only | The slug of the existing record that now carries the answer. |
| `merged_into` | `merged` only | The slug of the existing record this subject was folded into. |

No other key is allowed, at the top level or in an evidence item. A record must be a regular file: a symlinked record is refused. The filename without `.md` is the slug: lowercase kebab-case (`^[a-z0-9]+(-[a-z0-9]+)*$`). There are no numbers. The body has no required sections; Decision, Rationale, Boundary, and Consequences are common headings.

### Statuses

| Status | Meaning |
| --- | --- |
| `current` | This record holds the live answer for its subject. |
| `superseded` | The subject moved to another slug, named by `superseded_by`. This record is a tombstone. |
| `merged` | The subject was folded into another slug, named by `merged_into`. This record is a tombstone. |
| `needs-decision` | A stub naming an open subject with no ratified answer yet. It carries provenance evidence but no live decision. |

ADR status words such as `accepted`, `proposed`, and `draft` are refused. When converting an accepted ADR into a record, use `current`.

### Relations

- `superseded_by` and `merged_into` each name one existing record, never the record itself.
- `supersedes` is a list (not a single slug) of existing records.
- `current` and `needs-decision` records carry neither `superseded_by` nor `merged_into`.
- `superseded` requires `superseded_by` and forbids `merged_into`; `merged` requires `merged_into` and forbids `superseded_by`.

### Evidence

Provenance is linked, never inlined. `kind` is one of `issue`, `pr`, `commit` (a GitHub number, URL, or SHA), `session-archive` (a path to an archived session artifact), `adr` (a frozen numbered ADR), `doc` (a repository document), or `url` (an external permalink). `ref` is a non-blank string. A ref containing a secret-shaped literal is refused: an AWS access or STS key id, a GitHub token, a private key header, a JWT, or a quoted `secret`, `password`, `token`, or `api key` assignment.

### How the frontmatter is read

The block opens with a `---` line at byte 0, with no byte order mark, and ends at the next line that is `---` once trimmed. It is parsed as YAML with the failsafe schema, so every scalar is a string: `ref: 310` is the string `"310"`, and `decided: 2026-07-03` stays a string. A block that is not a mapping, repeats a key, or uses YAML anchors, aliases, or explicit tags is refused.

This replaces an earlier line-based parser. All 97 records in the seven registries that used it read identically under both. On other input the YAML reading wins, and it differs in both directions.

Now refused, where the earlier parser accepted the text literally:

- an unquoted `#` after a space starts a comment, so `ref: #310` is an empty ref and is refused (quote it: `ref: "#310"`);
- a plain value that YAML cannot read as a plain scalar: one containing `: ` (`subject: Release: channels`), one starting with a reserved character (`` ` ``, `@`, `%`), or one starting with a quote but continuing past it (`subject: "a" and "b"`). Quote the whole value;
- a value starting with `[` or `{` that is not a valid flow collection, or one that is a mapping where a string belongs (`subject: {x}`);
- repeated keys (the earlier parser kept the last one), tab indentation, anchors, aliases, and explicit tags;
- a tab or other control character inside a subject;
- an empty `supersedes:` (the earlier parser read it as an empty list);
- a subject whose value contains a line break: a double-quoted escape (`"C:\new"`), a literal block scalar (`|-` with two lines), or any block scalar that keeps its final line break (`>` or `|` without the `-` strip indicator). A subject merely written over several lines is different; see below.

Now accepted, where the earlier parser refused the line:

- a trailing comment (`status: current # note`), a space before the colon (`status : current`), and quoted keys (`"status": current`);
- flow mappings (`- { kind: pr, ref: "#1" }`, or `evidence: [{ kind: pr, ref: "#1" }]`);
- values continued over several lines, and a blank line inside an evidence item. A plain or quoted subject continued on an indented line, or a `>-` folded block without blank lines, is folded into one line (`First line second line`), so it is a valid single-line subject;
- block scalars (`>` and `|`) in fields other than `subject`.

Quoted strings are also unescaped (`"a \"b\""` is `a "b"`, and `'it''s'` is `it's`), so an index row can read differently from the earlier generator's output for a record written that way.

## The index

`corpus decisions index` writes the index, and no other file:

```markdown
---
title: Decision Index
---

# Decision Index

Generated by `corpus decisions index`. Do not edit by hand.
Topic-keyed living decision records; the format is described at https://github.com/kontourai/corpus/blob/main/docs/decisions.md.
Numbered ADRs under `docs/adr/` are frozen history and are not listed here.

| Topic | Status | Decision |
| --- | --- | --- |
| [release-channels](./release-channels.md) | current | Release channels |
```

The ADR line appears only when `adr` is declared, with its directory. Rows are sorted by slug; the Decision column is the subject, with `|` escaped. Output is deterministic, so running the command twice changes nothing. The gate fails when the index is missing or differs from what the command would write. It refuses to write through a symlink anywhere on the index path, and it refuses to replace an existing non-empty file that does not begin with the generated `title: Decision Index` frontmatter (a BOM, CRLF line endings, and leading merge-conflict markers are tolerated), so a mistaken `index` setting cannot overwrite a record.

For the 97 existing records, the index is identical to the one the earlier per-repository generator wrote except for header lines 7 and 8, provided `adr` is declared. Without `adr`, line 9 (the ADR line, which the earlier generator always wrote) is also dropped.

## Numbered ADRs

Numbered ADR directories are frozen history. New decisions go to the registry, where existing ADRs can be cited as `adr` evidence. ADR files are never validated as records, and their numbers stay as they are.

With `adr` declared, `corpus check --base <ref>` and `corpus decisions check --base <ref>` run the **adr-freeze** gate. It lists the files added under `adr.dir` between the merge base of `<ref>` and `HEAD` (`git diff --diff-filter=A --no-renames <ref>...HEAD`) and fails, exit `1`, for each one, naming the registry path to use instead. Editing an existing ADR, for a typo or a link, passes, and so does deleting one. Renaming a file inside `adr.dir` adds a path, so it fails.

Two names are exempt, so the directory can explain itself: `README.md` and `index.md`, directly in `adr.dir`, exactly as written. Any other added file fails, whatever its name or extension, including a `readme.md`, a `README.md` in a subdirectory, and a file renamed from an exempt name to an ADR name. The freeze uses this fixed list rather than freezing only files that look numbered (`NNNN-*.md`): a numbering pattern would let through every ADR added under another name (`adr-0005.md`, `0005_title.md`, a subdirectory), while the list admits two known names. An exempt file can still hold a decision, but there are two of them and both are visible in review. Renaming an existing ADR to an exempt name passes, because deleting an ADR passes; nothing new is admitted. Without `--base`, the gate is reported as `SKIP` with a note, because there is nothing to compare against. Uncommitted files are not seen; pull request CI, which passes `--base`, is where the freeze applies.

## Commands

```sh
corpus decisions check [--root dir] [--base <git-ref>]
corpus decisions index [--root dir]
```

`corpus decisions check` validates the manifest, then runs only the **decisions** gate (every record, then the index) and, when `adr` is declared, the **adr-freeze** gate. It reads no other document, so it is fast enough for a repository's own required lane. `corpus check` runs the same gates among the others, and `corpus build` runs the decisions gate (without the freeze). Exit codes match `check`: `0` ok, `1` a gate failed, `2` a usage or configuration error, including an invalid manifest, a `--base` that does not resolve (checked even when `adr` is not declared), and a manifest without a `decisions` block.

The shared Docs gate runs `corpus check`, so it picks up the gate wherever the manifest declares `decisions`. Where that job is not a required check, keep `corpus decisions check` in the repository's required lane, for example as the `check:decisions` script.

## Schema and conformance vectors

[`schemas/decision-record.schema.json`](../schemas/decision-record.schema.json) is the JSON Schema for the frontmatter, shipped in the package as `@kontourai/corpus/schemas/decision-record.schema.json`. Corpus enforces it, plus what a schema cannot state: the filename slug, relations to other records, the index, and the freeze.

[`@kontourai/corpus-conformance`](../packages/conformance/README.md#decision-record-vectors) ships `decision-records.json`, whole-registry vectors with the expected rule codes, so another validator can be tested against the same cases. Each of the six secret detectors has its own vector. Reachability, publishing, and the ADR freeze are repository checks, not part of the record format, so the vectors do not cover them.

The library exports `parseDecisionRecord(text)`, `validateDecisionRecord(slug, frontmatter, knownSlugs)`, `validateDecisions(root, decisions)`, and `renderDecisionIndex(records)`.

topics.title: docs-bundle.json format
topics.markdown:
## docs-bundle.json

Schema v2 adds `purpose` and `builtOn` from the manifest. `build` runs `check`, which refuses the exact placeholder `purpose` that `corpus init` writes, so a scaffolded sentence never reaches a built bundle. The MCP reader and hub accept both v1 and v2 bundles; v1 has no purpose metadata. `build` writes only v2 bundles, because only v2 manifests are read; v1 bundles that were published earlier stay readable. The bundle's `schemaVersion` is its own contract, separate from the manifest's. `list_products` includes both new fields for v2 bundles. `via` is a string or a non-empty array of package/CLI strings grouped under a declared product id. Package-to-product ownership and product ids are not verified offline. A building block may include `"evidence": "cli"`; the manifest check verifies its `via` command in package scripts or workflow run steps and keeps the reason in `for`. An optional bare `bin` string names a CLI executable differing from the `via` package name; it is invocation evidence, not verified package-to-bin ownership. GitHub expression values are neutralised before checking invocations; an untokenisable command line provides no evidence, other lines of the same step still do, and the failure names the skipped lines. This metadata is preserved in the bundle and accepted by MCP readers. Other evidence values are configuration errors.

The content digest algorithm remains unchanged; it identifies document content, not product metadata.

```json
{
  "schemaVersion": 2,
  "purpose": "Make process and execution state visible to users.",
  "builtOn": [],
  "product": "flow",
  "title": "Flow",
  "tagline": "Process transparency for agentic work",
  "repo": "kontourai/flow",
  "sha": "<git rev-parse HEAD at build time>",
  "builtAt": "2026-10-10T12:00:00.000Z",
  "siteUrl": "https://kontourai.github.io/flow/",
  "digest": "<sha256 hex>",
  "documents": [
    { "source": "README.md", "section": null, "title": "Flow", "landing": true, "url": "https://kontourai.github.io/flow/index.html", "repoPath": "README.md", "lineOffset": 0, "markdown": "# Flow\n..." },
    { "source": "docs/getting-started.md", "section": "Start Here", "title": "Getting started", "landing": false, "url": "https://kontourai.github.io/flow/docs/getting-started.html", "repoPath": "docs/getting-started.md", "lineOffset": 4, "markdown": "# Getting started\n..." }
  ],
  "topics": [
    { "id": "workflows", "title": "Workflows", "source": "docs/concepts.md#workflows", "url": "https://kontourai.github.io/flow/docs/concepts.html#workflows", "markdown": "## Workflows\n..." }
  ]
}
```

- `documents[0]` is the landing page, with `landing: true` and `section: null`. The listed documents follow in manifest order, with `landing: false`. A document's `title` is the `title` set on its `documents` entry in `corpus.json`, if any. Otherwise it is its first Markdown H1 outside blockquotes and lists, then the text of the first raw-HTML `<h1>` that has text, then a simple front-matter `title:`, then the file name without `.md`. `markdown` is the source file as written, minus a leading YAML front-matter block.
- Each document's `url` is the page `build` generates: `index.html` for the landing page, otherwise the source path with `.md` replaced by `.html`, under `siteUrl`. A [bundle-only document](../README.md#bundle-only-documents) (`"publish": false`) has no page, so its `url` is `https://github.com/<repo>/blob/<sha>/<path>` (`HEAD` in place of `<sha>` when `mcp` serves a directory outside git), and its `markdown` has relative links made absolute (images and other embedded files to `https://raw.githubusercontent.com/<repo>/<sha>/<path>`), as are topics taken from it. Published documents keep their Markdown as written. Redirect stubs from the manifest's `redirects` are not listed; the bundle has no field for them. The manifest's `decisions` block is not in the bundle either; decision records reach it only as listed documents. Declaring `decisions` lets `check` treat the records and the index as reachable without a `documents` entry, but an unlisted record is still left out of the bundle and the site.
- `repoPath` and `lineOffset` (since 0.6.0) say where `markdown` sits in the repository: `repoPath` is the source path from the git top level (it differs from `source` only when `--root` is a subdirectory), and `lineOffset` is the number of front-matter lines stripped before `markdown`'s first line, so line N of `markdown` is line N + `lineOffset` of the file. The MCP [`locate`](../README.md#mcp-server) tool uses them for file line numbers and GitHub links. Both are optional for readers: a bundle built before 0.6.0 has neither, and `locate` then assumes no front matter and says so. Neither is part of `digest`.
- A topic may carry three optional hierarchy fields: `parentId`, the `id` of another topic in the same bundle; `tags`, an array of non-empty strings; and `summary`, a string. `corpus build` does not write them yet; a host that generates its own bundle (for example, from a catalog of synthesized topics) does. The sources that serve written bundles validate them: a `parentId` that names no topic in the bundle, a chain of parents that loops, or a topic `id` used twice makes the bundle malformed, so `mcp --hub` reports the product unavailable and `mcp --bundle` (and `staticSource`) refuse it. `mcp --repo` and `--workspace` build their bundles from `corpus.json`, which cannot declare these fields and already refuses repeated topic ids. A topic without `parentId` is a root. `list_topics` returns the fields and filters by `parentId`; `search` scores a tag hit like an id hit (3) and a summary hit at 2, between a title (5) and a body (1) hit.
- A topic's `markdown` is a heading section: it runs from the anchor heading up to the next top-level heading of the same or a higher level. Deeper headings stay in the section. A topic without an anchor gets the whole document.
- `tagline` is `""` when the manifest omits it.
- `digest` is the SHA-256 (hex) of `JSON.stringify({documents, topics})`. Documents are reduced to `{source, section, title, landing, markdown}` and topics to `{id, title, source, markdown}`, followed by `parentId`, `tags`, and `summary` in that order when a topic has them (so a bundle without them hashes as it always did), in manifest order, with `markdown` as written (before bundle-only link rewriting, which embeds the sha and site URL). URLs, `sha`, and `builtAt` are left out, so the digest identifies the content alone.
- The hub's `thin` state and the MCP `docCount` count only documents with `landing: false`.

`mcp --bundle <file>` reads a written bundle once at startup and serves it unchanged until the server exits; a malformed one, or two for one product, is a usage error (exit `2`). `mcp --repo` and `mcp --workspace` build the same object in memory on every tool call. They read only `corpus.json` and refuse a retired `docs-kit.json`; `--workspace` serves each immediate subdirectory that has `corpus.json`, skips one with only `docs-kit.json` (noting it once on stderr), and reports a directory that has both as unavailable. Outside a git checkout, their `sha` is `null`. They add `dirty: true` when the working tree has uncommitted changes. The MCP server validates every bundle down to each document and topic; a malformed one is reported as unavailable.

topics.title: How links are rewritten on the site
topics.markdown:
## Link rewriting

| Link in Markdown | On the site |
| --- | --- |
| a published document (`concepts.md#workflows`) | the generated page (`concepts.html#workflows`) |
| the landing page (`../README.md`) | `index.html` |
| a local image | the copied image |
| a bundle-only document (`"publish": false`), or any other repository file or directory | `https://github.com/<repo>/blob/<sha>/<path>`, or `tree` for directories |
| `http(s):` and `mailto:` | unchanged |
| other schemes, such as `javascript:` | `#` |

The same rewriting applies to `href`, `src`, `srcset`, and `poster` attributes in raw HTML, in any quoting style. Raw HTML is tokenized with htmlparser2, so comments and quoting follow the HTML tokenizer, and `srcset` is parsed per the HTML spec. References to untracked, ignored, or `.git/` files fail `check` and `build`. `check` and `build` use one shared extractor for them.

topics.title: Known limits
topics.markdown:
## Known limits

- External links are never fetched, so a dead `https://` link passes `check`.
- `#fragment` matching is case-sensitive.
- Headings that contain images or code spans can slug slightly differently from github.com in edge cases.
- Links cannot point above `--root`, and a leading `/` resolves from `--root`, not from the git top level.
- Freshness is file-level: any edit to a covering document in the range counts as an update.
- Topic anchors must be headings outside blockquotes and lists. A heading inside a quote or a list item does not qualify, at any heading level.
- Mermaid diagrams need JavaScript and jsDelivr. Without them the page shows the diagram source as preformatted text.
- Raw-HTML `name` attributes count as anchors in `check`, but the sanitizer keeps `name` only on `<a>`. A `name` on another element passes `check` and then fails the generated-site check in `build`. Element `id`s are not prefixed with `user-content-` as they are on GitHub.
- MCP `search` is plain term matching with no stemming or synonyms.
- The hub calls the GitHub API without authentication, which allows 60 requests per hour per IP. The 10-minute `localStorage` cache keeps normal use within that limit.
- Any asset reference that goes through a symlink, as a file or as a directory in its path, is refused as unpublishable, whatever the link points at. Commit the real file instead.
- "Tracked" means present in the git index. A local `build` publishes tracked assets with their unstaged working-tree edits. CI builds from a clean checkout, so its output matches the commit.
- Empty directories that someone adds by hand inside the output directory are removed on rebuild. Only files are checked against the `.docs-kit-build` manifest.
- In a bundle-only document, a link destination written with backslash escapes (such as `[x](a\(b\).md)`) cannot be located in the source text, so it is left relative in the bundle. A topic's Markdown does not carry reference definitions from outside its section, so `[text][ref]` links in a topic stay unresolved.
- The paths gate matches home directories by shape. It does not catch a path relative to `~`, a percent-encoded path, or a home directory outside `/Users`, `/home`, and `C:\Users`.
- The selection toolbar's line ranges cover whole annotated blocks (a top-level paragraph, list item, table row, code block, or blockquote), not the selected characters. Raw HTML blocks have no line attribute, so a selection inside one carries only the page's path and sha.
- `locate` matches letters and digits, so it cannot tell apart passages that differ only in punctuation, and text that renders differently from its source (an image's alt text, a Mermaid diagram) needs the head-and-tail fallback.
- WebMCP is a Chromium-only draft whose API is still changing; the in-page tools follow the October 2026 draft and the earlier synchronous form, and may need updating as it evolves.
- The hub's install snippet shows `<sha>` as a placeholder. It cannot know which corpus commit to recommend.

topics.title: Mutable record store
topics.markdown:
# Corpus Store

`@kontourai/corpus-store` owns transactional, file-backed mutable records. Its
purpose is to give hosts one implementation of record identity, links,
provenance, mutations and recoverable publication. Immutable docs bundles are
separate. The docs CLI does not depend on this package and needs no build.

The extraction preserved Station semantics at
`2479f38b1ab062e2d9cd6df9f8fa2cdbeee1d136`; its only codec change preserves text
scalars from old Knowledge Kit writers. Later changes implement the owner's
decisions one at a time; see [Owner decisions](#owner-decisions). Version
`0.1.0-next.4` is intended for the `next` npm dist-tag through the
[workspace publish workflow](../../README.md#publishing-the-store-workspaces).

## Owner decisions

The [conformance vectors](../conformance/README.md) encode the owner's
2026-10-13 and 2026-11-02 decisions. A decision not yet implemented is an
explicit entry in [the expected-fail list](test/expected-fails.json), never
silent behavior.

- **Proposals may target any record type.** `propose`, `apply` and `reject`
  accept a target of every type, not only `concept`. The target and proposer
  must exist (`NOT_FOUND`), evidence fields are still required
  (`MISSING_EVIDENCE`), and `apply` and `reject` still require the proposer's
  `proposes` link to the target. Mutation-log evidence keeps its stored
  `concept_id` key.

- **Lists return the working set.** `listByType` and `listByCategory` omit
  retired and superseded records unless `includeHistory: true` is passed. Both
  profiles share one predicate: a record is historical when its status is
  `retired`, when it carries a `superseded-by` mutation-log entry, or (vault)
  when its note is archived. `implemented` records stay in the working set.
  The vault's history walks archived notes. `includeRetired` is a deprecated
  alias, translated to `includeHistory: true`, so it now also returns superseded
  records; removing the alias is a separate, owner-approved change. `get` and
  `getLinks` always reach history.

- **One expiry rule and an expiry-only stale filter.** A record expires at its
  explicit `expires_at`, otherwise `ttl_seconds` after `created_at`; a record
  with neither never expires. The TTL anchor is creation, so an update never
  extends it, and a record is expired from its expiry instant onward. List
  option `stale: true` keeps only expired records and `stale: false` only
  unexpired ones; without `stale` there is no expiry filter. `now` (epoch
  milliseconds) defaults to the injected `clock`. A non-boolean `stale` or a
  non-finite `now` is refused with `MISSING_EVIDENCE`. The filter composes with
  the working set. This is record expiry only: no `stale` status is stored,
  and maintenance age and trust freshness are separate signals.

- **A compiled record must link a raw source when it is created.** `create`
  with `type: 'compiled'` requires at least one link of kind `source` to an
  existing `raw` record; otherwise it throws `MISSING_EVIDENCE` and writes
  nothing. `provenance.source_ids`, `related` links and body wikilinks do not
  count. Only creation is checked: existing compiled records without a source
  stay readable, listable and updatable.

- **Erase a record with `purge`; erase a proposal with `purgeProposal`.**
  *(2026-11-02; this
  reverses the earlier rule that no operation deletes a record.)* `purge(ids,
  {agent, rationale, note?})` is an explicit, audited, privileged operation, and
  supersede stays the default for ordinary change. The owner's conditions: it is
  explicit and audited, it is privileged, supersede remains the default, and the
  tombstone keeps no plain content hash.

  - **Privileged.** The store cannot tell who may erase. `purge` is on a separate
    type, `KnowledgeStorePurger`, and an adapter refuses it with `READ_ONLY`
    before any I/O unless the host built it with `allowPurge: true`, which a host
    sets only after its own authorization. `agent` and `rationale` are required.
    The agent, rationale and note are retained as audit evidence: never put erased text in them.
  - **Targets.** Exact record ids only, never aliases or prefixes. Every id must
    exist (`NOT_FOUND`) or nothing is written. An identifiable proposal id gets
    a `purgeProposal` hint under the same code. Purging a tombstone again is a
    no-op that reports it in `alreadyPurged`.
  - **Tombstone.** Each target and each cascaded record is rewritten in place
    with `status: purged`. It keeps `id`, `type`, `created_at`, provenance
    (`agent`, `session_id`, `source_ids`), link targets and kinds, and its
    mutation log reduced to `op`, `at`, `agent` plus identity references. It ends
    with a `purged` entry holding `agent`, `rationale`, `note` and the cause:
    `requested`, or `sole-support-purged` with the support (`via`) that went. It
    drops title (now `[purged]`), body, tags, aliases, expiry, link labels,
    provenance `note`, the free-text log fields (`note`, `rationale`, proposal
    and reason text, link labels) and every unknown frontmatter field. Its
    category becomes `purged`, because a category path can name a data subject.
    **No content hash is kept**, not even of the title: for short content a hash
    lets anyone holding the tombstone confirm a guess. A keyed integrity
    reference may be added by a later, owner-approved change; today there is
    none. Surface#351 calls this retention state `deleted`; the stored
    `status: purged` is the same fact, and the id, provenance and `purged` entry
    are the erasure trace it asks for.
  - **Cascade.** Erasing a source also erases affected records that have no other
    remaining support. Records with other support stay; review them for leftover text.
    `cascaded` lists records erased with the requested records; `survivors` lists
    records kept because they have other support. A record's support is `provenance.source_ids` plus the targets of
    its `source` links. `related`, `proposes` and `supersedes` links are
    references, not support. A record is *affected* when a chain of support
    reaches a requested id. An affected record is tombstoned unless it still has
    real support: an id that is not a record in the store (an outside
    conversation id, say), a record the purge does not reach, or an affected
    record that itself survives. This is a least fixed point, so the cascade is
    transitive, and affected records that only support each other fall together
    instead of holding each other up. A record the purge does not reach is left
    alone, whatever its own support looks like.
  - **Survivors.** A record with other support survives untouched except for two
    things. Its log gains a `support-purged` entry (`agent`, `rationale`, the
    purged ids), and the labels of its links to erased records are dropped,
    because a label can repeat the erased title. A record that only links to an
    erased record gets the same label change and a `reference-purged` entry.
    `PurgeResult` lists `purged`, `cascaded`, `survivors`, `referrers` and
    `alreadyPurged`. The store does not scrub survivor *content* that may
    reproduce erased content; review those ids. Surface#351 splits the work the
    same way: the store represents the erasure, the producer removes
    reproductions.

    In a vault, a survivor or referrer is re-rendered and gains a log entry, which
    can grow a note that already sits near the vault note limit (16 MiB, see the
    note-limit decision), and every note a purge writes is held to that limit
    because a note over it breaks each later `create`. A survivor is the host's
    content, so the purge never shortens it: it first tries the entry without its
    `rationale` and `note` (`compact: true`), and if even that does not fit it
    refuses the whole purge with `MISSING_EVIDENCE`, names the record, and writes
    nothing, so the erasure waits until the host shrinks that note. A tombstone is
    different, because nothing the host does to a record changes what the
    tombstone must keep, and erasure must always be possible. A tombstone that
    would pass the limit (a note made mostly of provenance ids) falls back to a
    `purged` entry without `via` and with the rationale cut to 256 bytes as JSON
    (`compact: true`, and `rationale_truncated` and `rationale_bytes` when it was
    cut), and then to identity plus that entry with the rationale cut to 64 bytes
    and counts of what it dropped (`omitted_source_ids`, `omitted_links`,
    `omitted_log_entries`). In that last shape an agent, session id, `type` or
    `created_at` over 256 bytes as JSON is replaced (`[omitted]`, dropped, or the
    purge time) and counted (`omitted_agent_bytes`, `omitted_session_id_bytes`,
    `omitted_type_bytes`, `omitted_created_at_bytes`). A rationale is therefore
    never empty, so a consumer that needs a reason for the erasure always has
    one. The default layout has no such limit and always writes the full
    tombstone. **This is a narrow departure from "a tombstone keeps provenance,
    links and a purge entry", made so that erasure is not blocked**: it applies
    only when the full tombstone would exceed 16 MiB or cannot be written (the
    YAML writer overflows its stack on a multi-megabyte field), which needs a
    note made mostly of metadata, and what was lost is counted in the entry. A record id cannot be dropped, and the vault does not cap it as the
    default layout does ([#58](https://github.com/kontourai/corpus/issues/58)),
    so a purge of a record whose id alone fills the limit is still refused. The
    owner may prefer to refuse every such purge instead; that is a one-line
    change in `fittingTombstone`. Whether a consumer such as Surface needs a
    different bounded rationale is tracked in
    [#57](https://github.com/kontourai/corpus/issues/57).
  - **A tombstone is permanent and read-only.** `update`, `link`, `propose`,
    `apply`, `reject`, `supersede` and `retire` refuse it with `PURGED`, so do
    new `source` links, `source_ids` and compiled sources that name it, and its
    id cannot be created again. `get` returns it and `getLinks` keeps its link
    ids; lists treat it as history, so only `includeHistory: true` returns it,
    with no content.
  - **Create proposals.** A proposal holds its whole candidate in every state, in
    `.corpus-proposals/`, so a purge erases proposals itself. A proposal's support is
    its candidate's `provenance.source_ids` plus its `source` links, as for a record.
    One that rests only on erased records (support that is non-empty, entirely erased
    and including one this purge erases) is erased; a pending one is also settled as
    `rejected` by the purging agent with the purge's rationale, so it can never apply
    (`proposalsRejected`). An applied proposal is erased when the record it created
    is purged, and a rejected one when it rests only on erased records
    (`proposalsScrubbed`, which includes the rejected ones). Erasing keeps `id`,
    `state`, `proposer_id`, `evidence.agent`, the settlement identity and times, the
    candidate's type, provenance and link targets, and `record_id`; it replaces the
    title, body, category and `evidence.proposal` (and a settled rationale) with
    `[purged]`/empty, drops tags, aliases, expiry and link labels, and adds
    `erasure` (`at`, `agent`, `rationale`, `note`). A pending proposal with support
    left stays pending and is listed as `proposalsBlocked`: `applyCreate` refuses it
    with `PURGED` because its candidate still cites an erased record, and a reviewer
    can reject it to prevent application, but rejection leaves its text stored. Use
    `purgeProposal` if that text must be erased. `proposeCreate` refuses such a candidate up front, and also a candidate whose
    provenance (`agent`, `session_id`, `note`, `source_ids`) or links hold anything but text,
    or a link has an empty `target_id` or `kind` (the reader refuses such a record;
    [#56](https://github.com/kontourai/corpus/issues/56) tracks `create` itself)
    (purge reads them to decide what rests on what, and `create` would quietly turn a
    number into text), so no accepted proposal can stop a later purge. The
    log entry a created record starts with keeps `proposal_id` but never the
    proposal's text once the record is erased. A candidate's own `id` is not removed
    from its support (it is not a record yet, so it counts as real support until a
    record has it). A proposal whose stored shape purge cannot judge (unreadable,
    a candidate without valid provenance or links, an `erasure` marker over intact
    content) stops the purge before anything is written. Because a pending
    proposal's rejection copies the purge's `agent` (twice), `rationale` (twice) and
    `note` into it, those are bounded as JSON: `agent` 1 KiB, `rationale` and `note`
    8 KiB each (a control character is six bytes in JSON), which fits the 64 KiB a
    stored proposal reserves for settlement.
  - **Read paths and projections.** The slug aliases leave the alias index, the
    graph index rebuilds from tombstone links, and `reindex` reproduces the same
    result. In the vault the file moves to `archive/purged/<id>.md` (so the path
    index is never empty after a purge, and a vault whose only record was purged
    still opens, lists and reindexes; the empty-vault rule of
    [#50](https://github.com/kontourai/corpus/pull/50) never applies to it), the path
    index loses the title slug, category folders the purge emptied are removed,
    and every record that linked to it is re-rendered, so no generated `[[link]]`
    section still names the erased title. The `dimensions` frontmatter is not written to a tombstone.
  - **Recoverable publication.** The transaction journal holds base64
    before-images of every file it touches so an interrupted write can roll
    back. For a purge, the commit marker drops them, so a journal left by a
    crash after the commit marker holds no erased content. A purge does not
    report success while its journal may still hold them: if the commit marker
    cannot be written, it removes the journal or throws. The next locked
    operation also removes a `.<id>.tmp` file that a crash inside the journal's
    own write left at the root, even a cut-short one, but only one that starts
    the way this engine writes a journal (a stray file with exactly that start
    would be removed too). A failure to remove it fails the operation, so a store
    stays unavailable until the file can be deleted. Emptied folders are removed
    best effort after the commit, and a path component that is a symlink stops
    the removal; as with the engine's other path checks, this assumes nothing
    else swaps a store folder for a symlink in the moment between the check and
    the removal, which the store lock cannot prevent.
    *Deferred:* between
    the first journal write and the commit marker the journal still holds the
    pre-purge files, because rollback needs them. A crash in that window leaves
    them on disk until the next locked read recovers it, and unlinking a file is
    not secure erasure. `purge-journal-in-flight` records this on the
    expected-fail list. Closing it needs a roll-forward journal, which is a
    separate change to the transaction engine.
  - **Migration artifacts.** A vault that still holds `.corpus-store-migration/`
    keeps the original Kit index (every path, so every title slug and category)
